title: refactor(ci): modernize build matrix, improve cache parallelism, and release automation hygiene
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Our CI workflows have grown organically over the past 18 months and suffer from long matrices, duplicated job definitions across repos, and sub-optimal cache behavior that increases total build time and costs. This PR modernizes the GitHub Actions build matrix, centralizes cache keys and pruning logic, and makes small release automation hygiene fixes to reduce noise and improve reliability.

What changed (high level):
- Consolidated duplicate matrix permutations into a single reusable matrix template (github/workflows/ci-matrix.yml) and introduced explicit cohorts for lint/unit/integration to reduce unnecessary combinations.
- Reworked cache key strategy: use language/hash of lockfile + job-role prefix + runner-label to avoid cross-job contamination; added a parallel restore/restore-fallback flow to reduce cold-cache misses.
- Added a cache pruning action (scripts/ci/prune-cache.sh) that runs weekly and prunes stale branch caches older than 30 days to limit disk usage on self-hosted runners.
- Split long-running integration jobs onto a dedicated job group with a lower concurrency and explicit retry; moved ephemeral network e2e to `canary` workflow to reduce noise in PR checks.
- Release automation hygiene: small fixes to .github/workflows/release.yml to stop duplicate changelog generation, improve tagging semantics, and add a guard for missing GITHUB_TOKEN scopes.

Files touched (representative): .github/workflows/ci-matrix.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml, .github/actions/cache/entrypoint.sh, scripts/ci/prune-cache.sh, package.json (ci scripts), .github/workflows/canary-e2e.yml, docs/ci/README.md, .github/labels/ci.yml

Checklist:
- [x] Matrix consolidated and verified locally via act and on a feature branch run.
- [x] Cache keys validated across Linux/Mac runners and self-hosted pool.
- [x] Weekly cache pruning job added and tested on staging runner.
- [x] Release workflow tested with dry-run tagging.
- [x] Metrics baseline captured for before/after comparison (see perf notes).

Testing and verification:
- Run summary: reduced total CI concurrency by ~28% on a representative large PR while keeping median PR feedback time stable. Cache hit rate increased from 62% to 84% on average in our self-hosted pool during feature branch runs.
- CI checks passed on the merge run after a single cache-fallback tweak (see commit history).

Backward compatibility / migration notes:
- This change is intended to be transparent for contributors. In rare cases where a job experiences a cache miss after the key strategy change, the fallback flow will populate a new cache without failing the job. Self-hosted runners should pick up the prune job but will not delete any caches younger than 30 days.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind a short maintenance window (low risk).
2) Monitor CI success rates and runner disk usage for 72 hours.
3) If we see regressions, rollback to previous workflow commit and revert PR.

Related: ENG-2045 (CI matrix modernization), ENG-2101 (cache strategy), SUP-4321 (support ticket about flaky e2e in PR checks).
